notes: Head 1 to 1 3/8 in (25–35 mm) from bottom of chin to top of head.
8 FAM 402.1-2 says head size is measured to the top of the head, not the applicant's hair; the public page says hair may extend past the photo edges as long as the entire head is shown.
Colour photo taken in the last 6 months; neutral expression or natural smile, eyes open, mouth closed.
No glasses unless they cannot be removed for medical reasons (signed doctor's note required).
No hats or head coverings except for religious or medical reasons (signed statement).
No filters, digital edits or AI enhancement.
The passport photo page gives no eye-line range; State Dept's visa photo template uses 1 1/8–1 3/8 in (28–35 mm) from the bottom.
Online renewal upload: JPG/JPEG/PNG/HEIC/HEIF, 54 KB–10 MB.
It is acceptable if a baby's (especially a newborn's) eyes are partially or completely closed; all other children must have eyes open.
Head may be discreetly supported, e.g. a car seat covered with a white or off-white blanket; head tilt is acceptable for infants.
No other person (including a parent's face or hands covering the face) may be in the photo; no pacifier covering the face.
The passport card uses the same photo standard as the passport book (8 FAM 402.1 applies to both); one 2 × 2 in photo with the DS-11/DS-82.
Head 1 to 1 3/8 in from bottom of chin to top of head (not hair).
Colour photo taken in the last 6 months; no glasses except for documented medical reasons.
Uniforms and military/law-enforcement-style clothing are not acceptable for passport books or cards.
Infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, may be partially or completely closed.
Head may be discreetly supported (e.g. car seat with a white or off-white blanket); head tilt is acceptable.
A parent's face cannot be in the photo.
Head (top of hair to bottom of chin) 1 to 1 3/8 in (25–35 mm) on paper, or 50%–69% of the digital image height.
Eye height 1 1/8 to 1 3/8 in (28–35 mm) from the bottom on paper, or 56%–69% of the digital image height.
DS-160 / DS-1648 digital upload: JPEG, square, minimum 600 × 600 px, maximum 1200 × 1200 px, ≤ 240 kB, sRGB 24-bit colour, compression ratio ≤ 20:1.
Diversity Visa entry: exactly 600 × 600 px JPEG, ≤ 240 kB.
Immigrant visa (DS-260) and DV selectees bring two identical 2 × 2 in printed photos.
Taken within the last 6 months; neutral expression, both eyes open.
Eyeglasses not allowed except in rare medical cases with a signed medical statement.
Babies must have eyes open in visa photos.
Passport-style photos: two identical colour photos, 2 × 2 in, full-face frontal view.
Head height 1 to 1 3/8 in from the top of the hair to the bottom of the chin; eye height 1 1/8 to 1 3/8 in from the bottom of the photo.
White to off-white background; printed on thin paper with a glossy finish; unmounted and unretouched; taken recently.
Head must be bare unless headwear is required by religious denomination.
Print name and A-Number lightly on the back in pencil or felt pen.
Used for Forms I-485, N-400 (when required), I-765 and similar. USCIS form instructions do not mention glasses; the State Department passport/visa standard bans them, so remove them.
Face height 31–36 mm (1¼–1 7/16 in) from chin to crown (top of head); IRCC defines crown as the top of the head/skull where hair obscures it.
Plain white or light-coloured background with clear contrast to the face.
Taken by a commercial photographer or studio, no more than 6 months before applying.
Neutral expression: eyes open and clearly visible, mouth closed, not smiling or frowning.
Glasses allowed if eyes are clearly visible with no glare; no sunglasses or tinted lenses.
Online renewal digital photo: JPEG, 3:2 portrait, 1200 × 1800 px to 3000 × 4500 px, 200 KB–5 MB, chin-to-crown 45%–50% of photo height.
IRCC allows some range of facial expression for newborns, but does not say eyes may be closed.
A newborn may be photographed in a car seat with a white blanket over the seat behind the head, with no shadows.
Head 31–36 mm from bottom of chin to top of head, not including hair.
Plain, untextured white background; no shadows on face, shoulders, around ears or in background.
Taken no more than 12 months before applying.
Glasses allowed if eyes are clearly visible with no glare.
Digital photo: JPEG, 715 × 1000 px to 2000 × 2800 px, 4 MB or less.
Photos printed at home on heavyweight paper are not accepted.
IRCC allows a range of facial expressions for newborns but does not say eyes may be closed.
Temporary resident visa: frame at least 35 × 45 mm; head 31–36 mm chin to crown.
Crown is the top of the head, or where the top of the skull would be if obscured by hair or head covering.
Plain white or light-coloured background.
Two identical photos taken within the last 6 months, on quality photographic paper; digital photos must not be altered.
Non-tinted prescription glasses allowed if eyes are clearly visible; no sunglasses.
Neutral expression, mouth closed, facing the camera.
Two identical colour photographs, matte/dull finish (PICA poster recommends semi-gloss, high-quality paper), taken no more than 6 months before the application.
Face length (chin to top of head) 25–35 mm; PICA web page gives a 3–4 mm margin between head and top edge, while the PICA photo poster says at least 2 mm from the top of the head (including hair).

Plain background with no shadows or objects. PICA advises: light complexion – pastel-shaded background and no white clothing; dark complexion – white background with coloured clothing; grey/white hair – pale blue or pastel background.
Neutral expression, no smiling; face square to the camera; eyes open, no hair across eyes or forehead; both ears visible as far as possible.
Glasses: no tinted lenses, no reflections, avoid heavy frames; PICA strongly recommends removing glasses.
Head covering only for religious reasons, with the face from chin to top of forehead visible.

One photo must be certified on the back by a Consular Officer, JP, Notary Public, Commissioner of Oaths, Medical Doctor or Lawyer (certification not older than 6 months); no stamps or seals on the photo; do not staple or clip.
Online adult renewal (passport.pica-online.com) takes a digital photo checked by PICA's photo checker; exact pixel/file limits were not found on an official page.
Size stated as 31 mm wide × 41 mm high ('at least' in embassy instructions).
Head size: the source gives chin to crown (top of the head without hair) as 70–80% of the photo height, converted to 28.7–32.8 mm for a 41 mm photo.

First-time and in-country applicants have their photo taken live at the Immigration Office; printed photos are needed for renewals through missions abroad and for replacing a lost, stolen or damaged passport (one photo, solid white background).
Taken within the last 6 months; colour; neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open, facing square to the camera; no hair on forehead or over eyes/ears; both edges of face visible.
Spectacles are not acceptable in the portrait (2026 Ministry instructions).
Headdress only for religious or medical reasons; no facial markings, tattoos or piercings that obscure the face.
Do not pin, staple or glue photos; the recommender certifies the back of one photo; no notarial seals on photos.
Some missions set their own size: the Consulate General in New York asks for 2 × 2 in and Toronto asks for at least 5 × 5 cm; check with the mission you are applying through.
For passport renewals through the Consulate General of Trinidad and Tobago in New York (instructions updated January 2026): two passport photos.
Face size from crown to chin between 1 in and 1⅜ in (25.4–34.9 mm); the consulate says 'crown' and does not say whether hair is included.
Taken within the last 6 months; colour; plain white background; even lighting with no shadows or reflections.
No glasses or contact lenses; eyes open, mouth closed, neutral expression (no smiling), facing the camera squarely, head upright.
No hair covering forehead, eyes or ears; both edges of face and ears visible; headdress only for religious or medical reasons.
No facial jewellery, markings, tattoos or piercings that obscure the face; no camouflage prints; shoulders covered.

Printed photos are needed only when applying from abroad by mail/through a consulate without biometric equipment; in Panama (APAP) and at consulates with APAP equipment the photo is taken on site and no photos are needed.
Size 3.5 × 4.5 cm as stated by the Embassy of Panama in Germany (3 photos for adults, 4 for minors). The APAP data-capture form (Formato de captura de datos) has a portrait box labelled 4 × 5 cm.
Head size from ICAO guidance: Panama requires photos that meet ICAO (OACI) requirements; ICAO 9303 chin-to-crown 70–80% of photo height = 31.5–36 mm on a 45 mm photo.
Background must be completely white; colour photo.
Stand upright, centred, looking at the camera; ears visible.
Small earrings only; no hair clips or ribbons; no piercings; no glasses.
Smiling without showing teeth is accepted.
No low-cut tops or bare shoulders; embassy advises not wearing white and preferably tying long hair back.
Religious veils (face uncovered) and turbans are permitted.
